chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahbub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu al-Rabi' al-Shami, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he was asked about a man who said, 'Fasting is upon me for a time,' and that was in his doubt.

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, 'My father (peace be upon him) was asked about something similar, and he said, 'Fast for six months, for indeed Allah the Exalted says, "It yields its fruit at every time by the permission of its Lord."' He meant six months.'
ai.seo_question: How to fulfill a vow of fasting when the duration is unspecified or doubtful?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) resolves the ambiguity of a vow to fast 'for a time' by interpreting the Quranic phrase 'at every time' (bi-idhn rabbihā) as referring to six months, a duration derived from the linguistic nuance of the verse. This ruling exemplifies the Shia scholarly method of using Quranic exegesis to clarify legal uncertainties in personal vows (nadhr), linking the concept of divine permission for fruitfulness to a specific temporal period. The interpretation reflects the tradition of deriving practical jurisprudence from the semantic flexibility of Quranic expressions.
